newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus Amax Q2 hurt by interest costs.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax Q2 hurt by interest costs.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals Co Tuesday reported slightly lower second quarter earnings after special items, despite record copper production, citing increased interest payments.
These costs are expected to decline in the future, spokesman Mike Rounds said.
Net income rose to $66 million, or $0.65 per share, in the quarter from $53 million, or $0.52 per share, in 1996's second quarter.

In the latest quarter, Cyprus Amax said it recorded an after-tax gain of $19 million, or $0.cents per share, on the sale of the Kubaka mine to AMAX Gold Inc, and a charge of $5 million, or $0.05 per share, for the costs of the tender for its 9-7/8 percent debentures.
That left earnings per share at $0.51, still above the first call consensus of $0.47.
Cyprus Amax interest costs rose slightly in the latest quarter -- to $53 million from $45 million last year -- but the portion capitalized dropped to $2 million this year from $21 million in 1996.
The bottom-line interest cost was $51 million in 1997's second quarter and $24 million a year earlier.
Rounds attributed the drop in capitalized interest to the fact the company is in the final stages of its current capital spending cycle.

Cyprus Amax said copper production was a record 265 million pounds, "reflecting increases at our domestic operations and Cerro Verde, as well as the impact of El Abra. Our consolidated second quarter cash costs were $0.62 per pound, down $0.10 or 14 percent from last year."
Rounds said El Abra's cost is $0.35 per pound of copper.
The company said "Coal operating earnings improved substantially in the second quarter.
"Production records were set at six mines and productivity improved dramatically.

"With higher production, lower costs and lower capital requirements, we were able to complete a cash tender offer for about 70 percent of the $300 million in nine percent debentures due June 30, 2001," Cyprus Amax said. "By early July 1997, we reduced long-term debt by $294 million from December 31, 1996, or by about 12 percent."
